invariant: Captured provider cost cannot exceed the authorized hold.
Every quote identifies the price revision used to calculate its maximum charge.
cards.role: Quote a pinned price revision, authorize a bounded hold, capture provider usage once, and release the unused balance.

invariant: Evidence content is redacted before its digest, size, and token estimate are recorded.
Preview and build share the same selection and redaction path.
cards.role: Select, redact, hash, and package repository evidence before expert consultation data leaves the local boundary.

invariant: Only declared state-event pairs can advance a consultation.
cards.role: Define allowed consultation state transitions from context request through approval, execution, result, and terminal outcomes.

invariant: Reading and answering consultations require distinct explicit scopes.
Untrusted requests are bounded before reaching MCP handlers.
cards.role: Expose tenant-scoped remote expert tools behind bearer authentication, host, origin, body-size, and per-tool scope checks.

invariant: Strict conversion rejects fatal information loss.
cards.role: Decode provider ingress into canonical requests and encode canonical requests with explicit loss reports.

invariant: Configured routes reference enabled providers and supported protocols.
Expired signed runtime state prevents candidate selection.
cards.role: Build and serve validated provider candidates for virtual and direct model routes under runtime availability state.

invariant: No retry starts after an attempt has committed a semantic event.
Each attempted candidate is excluded before another retry.
cards.role: Coordinate candidate selection, lease acquisition, provider attempts, commit hooks, and retry termination for one canonical request.

invariant: Callers dial one of the already validated resolved addresses instead of repeating DNS lookup.
cards.role: Resolve provider and MCP destination hosts once and reject credentials, unsafe schemes, ports, and non-public addresses before dialing.

invariant: PostgreSQL stores only a peppered secret digest and the plaintext secret is returned only when a key is issued.
Authentication compares secret digests in constant time and rejects expired, revoked, or wrong-environment keys.
cards.role: Issue, authenticate, authorize, and revoke project-scoped virtual keys without persisting plaintext secrets.
Verify issued virtual keys round-trip through authentication and malformed key material is rejected.

invariant: Control responses are size-bounded and valid JSON before they are printed or written atomically.
cards.role: Inspect signing keys, fetch signed snapshots and model catalogs, and publish reviewed control snapshots through the Control Plane API.

invariant: Non-public control operations pass authentication and authorization before snapshot state is read or changed.
cards.role: Run the authenticated Control Plane service that signs, publishes, and serves versioned runtime snapshots and model state.

invariant: Migration execution uses the ordered embedded migration set and a caller-bounded context timeout.
cards.role: Apply, inspect, or explicitly roll back the embedded RelayDock PostgreSQL migration sequence.

invariant: Consultation requests return durable identities while execution continues through the owned asynchronous runner.
cards.role: Run the expert consultation broker, persistence backend, asynchronous runner, HTTP API, and optional remote MCP endpoint.

invariant: Dry-run compaction reports the proposed changes without mutating local consultation state.
cards.role: Inspect, verify, and compact the local expert consultation store with explicit retention and dry-run controls.

invariant: Startup aborts when required database, secret, authentication, or runtime dependencies cannot be constructed safely.
cards.role: Run the authenticated AI gateway with provider routing, accounting, leases, runtime journaling, and signed control-state synchronization.

invariant: The headless process exposes the runtime only through the configured local IPC transport.
cards.role: Run the persistent local RelayDock runtime without a desktop UI and expose it through the platform-local IPC endpoint.

invariant: The plaintext virtual-key secret is emitted only by the issue command and is never read back from storage.
cards.role: Issue and revoke project-scoped gateway virtual keys against the authoritative PostgreSQL control store.

invariant: Stdout remains exclusive to MCP protocol traffic and diagnostics are written to stderr.
cards.role: Run the local MCP stdio bridge that delegates expert consultation tools to the RelayDock local IPC runtime.

invariant: Issued scopes and tenant or project constraints are validated and token lifetime cannot exceed the configured maximum.
cards.role: Issue bounded, audience-specific expert MCP bearer tokens with validated scopes and optional tenant or project constraints.

invariant: Mutating maintenance commands require explicit bounded targets and never claim ownership of in-flight events.
cards.role: Inspect durable outbox health, list dead letters, requeue one failed event, and purge bounded published history.

invariant: Delivery attempts flow through the durable outbox repository so retries do not bypass lease and attempt state.
cards.role: Run the durable outbox worker that leases pending events, publishes signed webhooks, and exposes bounded health status.

invariant: Organization and project creation commit together in one database transaction under validated stable slugs.
cards.role: Create or retrieve stable organization and project identities in the PostgreSQL control catalog.

invariant: Signing and verification are explicit subcommands over caller-selected release artifacts rather than implicit build side effects.
cards.role: Audit, build, sign, and verify RelayDock release bundles, checksums, readiness evidence, and update manifests.

invariant: Non-loopback binding requires bearer authentication and request bodies remain within the configured maximum.
cards.role: Run the reference signed-webhook receiver with bounded bodies, replay-safe verification, and authenticated non-loopback access.

invariant: Authentication establishes identity but never grants an action without an explicit authorization decision.
Tenant- or project-scoped principals cannot acquire cluster-wide publisher, gateway, or administrator authority.
cards.role: Establish Control Plane principals and make deny-by-default authorization decisions for every control action.
Verify the deny-by-default Control Plane role matrix and reject project-scoped privilege roles.

invariant: An unsigned, expired, rolled-back, or content-mutated revision is never applied as current runtime state.
A last-known-good persistence failure cannot replace or invalidate an already verified active snapshot.
cards.role: Verify, apply, persist, and refresh signed runtime snapshots while preserving a last-known-good fallback.
Verify snapshot rollback, same-revision mutation, and last-known-good persistence failure handling.

invariant: Stdout is reserved for MCP protocol messages and operational logs are written only to stderr.
Tool handlers delegate bounded operations to local IPC instead of running consultations synchronously.
cards.role: Expose local expert consultation operations as MCP stdio tools backed by the authenticated local IPC runtime.

invariant: Only the active key signs new tokens while retained keys are verification-only.
A verification key cannot replace the active key with different secret material.
cards.role: Rotate scoped-token signing keys while retaining bounded verification overlap and constant-time secret comparisons.
Verify scoped-token rotation overlap, audience and expiry enforcement, tamper rejection, key-map normalization, and claim size bounds.

invariant: Callers classify failures with errors.Is rather than matching message text.
New identities remain provider-neutral and preserve existing transport mappings.
cards.role: Define stable cross-layer error identities used for transport status mapping, retry decisions, and operator diagnostics.

invariant: Credential values are copied at ownership boundaries and cleared after transport use.
Remote D-Bus error bodies never enter public errors.
cards.role: Store opaque credential bytes in the Linux Secret Service through cancellable D-Bus sessions, unlock prompts, and bounded public errors.
Verify Linux Secret Service create, unlock, read, delete, cancellation, byte clearing, and remote error redaction behavior.

invariant: Durable stores use their atomic aggregate operations when available.
Fallback writes compensate partial ContextPack or result persistence on later failure.
cards.role: Compose expert consultation, ContextPack, and result stores while preserving atomic cross-aggregate creation and completion when supported.

invariant: A positive cost ceiling is enforced before network I/O using configured pricing.
Provider responses are bounded and must validate against the result contract.
cards.role: Submit a redacted ContextPack to the OpenAI Responses API under explicit output and cost ceilings, then validate the structured expert result.

invariant: Only a digest of each read token is retained after issuance.
Expired handoffs cannot resolve tokens or accept results.
cards.role: Issue expiring read tokens for browser handoff consultations and accept only validated structured results before expiry.

invariant: UI modules consume this adapter instead of importing generated bindings directly.
ContextPack previews use an explicit byte ceiling and report redaction findings.
cards.role: Keep desktop UI calls behind typed Wails service adapters and build privacy-aware ContextPack previews before consultation creation.

invariant: Connections beyond the configured concurrency bound are closed instead of queued without limit.
Malformed or oversized frames terminate the connection after one bounded error response.
cards.role: Serve bounded framed JSON requests over the local endpoint with explicit connection backpressure and method dispatch.

invariant: Foreign-key and check constraints are removed before their owned columns.
The initial consultation and ContextPack tables remain available after rollback.
cards.role: Remove expert durability indexes, lease metadata, tenant scope, and result linkage introduced by migration 000002.

invariant: Consultation attempt counts cannot become negative.
Queued and stale-running consultations have separate partial indexes for worker recovery.
cards.role: Add tenant scope, fenced worker lease state, result provenance, and claim indexes to durable expert consultations.

invariant: Rollback removes outbox, expert, runtime, and control schemas as one ordered migration step.
The public schema and migration runner ledger remain outside this rollback file.
cards.role: Remove every application schema created by the initial RelayDock migration during an explicit full rollback.

invariant: Usage events remain separate from request and provider-attempt records.
Consultation idempotency is unique within each project.
cards.role: Create the initial control, runtime, expert, and outbox PostgreSQL schemas and their foundational integrity constraints.

invariant: Delivery-specific indexes are removed before their backing columns.
The restored queue index continues to exclude published events.
cards.role: Remove recoverable lease and dead-letter state while restoring the initial pending-event queue index.

invariant: An event cannot be both published and dead-lettered.
Claim and stale-lock indexes exclude terminal events.
cards.role: Add recoverable outbox lease expiry, bounded failure state, dead-letter state, and worker-oriented partial indexes.

invariant: The NOT NULL provider connection constraint is restored only when no existing attempt contains NULL.
Base request and provider-attempt records survive the rollback.
cards.role: Remove expanded request usage and provider-attempt journal fields while restoring the original connection requirement when data permits.

invariant: Attempt and token counters remain non-negative.
Provider attempts may omit a control-plane connection when signed snapshots supply the route.
cards.role: Expand the runtime journal with client identity, tenant scope, usage totals, provider attempt provenance, commit state, and bounded failure metadata.

invariant: The completion closure exports a span at most once.
Exporter failures never replace the application operation result.
cards.role: Create process-local trace spans with parent propagation, exactly-once completion, and a replaceable exporter boundary.

imports: %w: outbox lease TTL %s must exceed publish timeout %s plus repository timeout %s
invariant: Lease TTL exceeds the combined publish and repository operation timeouts.
Every completion call includes the worker identity that owns the claim.
cards.role: Deliver leased outbox events with bounded concurrency, fenced completion, deterministic jitter, retry limits, and dead-letter handling.

invariant: Concurrent claims skip locked rows and preserve queue order among eligible events.
A stale or expired worker lease cannot complete an event.
cards.role: Lease PostgreSQL outbox events to workers and fence publish, retry, release, and dead-letter completion by the active lease owner.

invariant: The previous complete file remains recoverable until the replacement is installed.
Reads reject files larger than the caller limit before returning bytes.
cards.role: Persist bounded local state through a same-directory temporary file, durable flushes, restrictive permissions, and recoverable replacement.

invariant: Only one runner mutates the schema while the advisory lock is held.
Each migration step and its ledger update commit in the same transaction.
cards.role: Apply or roll back embedded PostgreSQL migrations in version order under one advisory lock with checksum validation.

invariant: Unknown extension payloads remain available as raw JSON for compatible conversion.
Every item kind must carry the fields required by its canonical meaning.
cards.role: Define the provider-neutral request vocabulary that preserves messages, tools, reasoning, capabilities, metadata, and unknown extensions.

invariant: Terminal streams reject every later event and cancellation.
Transparent retry becomes impossible after the first semantic event is accepted.
cards.role: Serialize canonical stream transitions and expose whether a failed attempt remains safe for transparent retry.

invariant: Routing policy does not depend on provider-specific error strings.
Provider messages are sanitized and bounded before entering structured errors.
cards.role: Normalize HTTP and transport failures into provider-neutral classes used by retry, cooldown, metrics, and public error codes.

invariant: Anonymous access is rejected unless the adapter configuration explicitly permits it.
Successful and error response bodies are read through fixed upper bounds.
cards.role: Execute provider-neutral HTTP attempts with configured authentication, protocol paths, bounded responses, and normalized upstream failures.

invariant: Request decoding rejects unknown fields, oversized bodies, and more than one JSON value.
Every JSON response is marked no-store.
cards.role: Enforce bounded single-value JSON requests and map RelayDock domain errors into no-store JSON responses.

invariant: Headers and the streaming status line are committed only once.
No semantic event is emitted before the upstream route commit hook succeeds.
cards.role: Commit provider metadata and translate canonical stream events into OpenAI-compatible live HTTP output without reopening retry eligibility.

invariant: The control bearer token is read only in the server loader and is never returned in page data.
Probe failures degrade to explicit offline or empty status without aborting the complete overview.
cards.role: Load authenticated health, readiness, model-route, and signed-snapshot status for the server-rendered control overview.

invariant: Invalid results are rejected before an identifier is allocated or a record is stored.
Stored and returned results are cloned so callers cannot mutate retained records through shared maps or slices.
cards.role: Normalize, validate, clone, and store expert result records behind process-local Store and RecordStore contracts.

invariant: SIGINT or SIGTERM starts one graceful shutdown with a bounded fifteen-second budget.
http.ErrServerClosed is treated as an expected terminal state rather than a runtime failure.
cards.role: Run RelayDock HTTP handlers with bounded header reads, idle connections, signal cancellation, and graceful shutdown.

invariant: The encoded identifier contains no padding and remains safe in URLs and filenames.
A requested prefix is preserved before one underscore without changing the sortable timestamp portion.
cards.role: Generate optional-prefixed, sortable, URL-safe identifiers for RelayDock records and leases.

invariant: Candidate slices are copied at the store boundary so callers cannot mutate retained routing state.
Expired leases are pruned before capacity, renewal, release, or active-count decisions.
cards.role: Provide process-local health candidates and expiring account concurrency leases for single-runtime routing.
